Summary: Derek grows more untethered the closer it gets to Stiles leaving for college, tossing and turning at night, unable to sleep with the preemptive ache of anxiety and loss in his chest. Then Stiles is gone, too many miles away, out of Derek’s arms. Derek yearns for him, misses him like an absent limb, treasures his voice over the phone like an anchor. He makes do with Stiles talking to him, telling him stories and helping him fall asleep with his voice alone, clinging onto the memory of Stiles’ fingers stroking through his hair and his lips on Derek’s forehead, until the next time they meet.
